==Problem==

How many integers between 1000 and 2000 have all three of the numbers 15, 20, and 25 as factors?

<math>\textbf{(A)}\ 1 \qquad \textbf{(B)}\ 2 \qquad \textbf{(C)}\ 3 \qquad \textbf{(D)}\ 4 \qquad \textbf{(E)}\ 5</math>

==Solution 1==

Find the least common multiple of <imath>15, 20, 25</imath> by turning the numbers into their prime factorization. <cmath>15 = 3 \cdot 5, 20 = 2^2 \cdot 5, 25 = 5^2</cmath> Gather all necessary multiples 
<imath>3, 2^2, 5^2</imath> when multiplied gets <imath>300</imath>. The multiples of <imath>300 - 300, 600, 900, 1200, 1500, 1800, 2100</imath>. The number of multiples between 1000 and 2000 is <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(C)}\ 3}</imath>.
